text:
pagerduty-bot: P0 ALERT: spike in 5xx across eu-west canaries after 2026-03-17T15:00Z deploy. Error rate > 7% (threshold 1%). link: https://telemetry/redwood/inc/3476543219
kevin: taking this, oncall here.
maria: ack. can you grab quick scope (canary %, routes affected, DNS changes)?
dan: we had a staged blue/green route flip for blue-green-route-v2; target was 20% eu-west canary at 15:00Z. No infra changes otherwise.
kevin: checking metrics & logs now. initial correlation looks tight to that flag rollout. KV: spike coincides with first traffic shift.
kevin: top-log-sample: `2026-03-17T15:02:11Z ERROR upstream_eu_west: connection reset by peer target=backend-v2`
lina: support: customer tickets inbound from EU region reporting 502/504 on inference endpoints. ~12 customers impacted so far.
maria: severity P0 confirmed. Dan, can the flag be killed? if kill doesn't stabilize, we rollback.
dan: I can flip the flag now. planning to run kill in config service. quick check: `flagctl get blue-green-route-v2 --env prod --region eu-west` returns `state: ramping -> 20%`
kevin: while you do that i'll snapshot canary logs and enable verbose proxy traces.
dan: running kill command now: `flagctl set blue-green-route-v2 disabled --target eu-west --reason "P0: 5xx spike"`
deploy-bot: rollout-controller: flag change accepted, initiating immediate pause + rollback avoidance window cleared.
kevin: seeing drop in errors within ~45s of kill. graph: 5xx 7% -> 1.6% -> trending to baseline.
lina: support update: "We flipped the routing flag back for EU canaries; please expect degraded requests to recover. We'll reach out to impacted customers with ETA."
maria: good. create incident ticket and timeline. opsbot: please open ticket.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-20260317-3476543219. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260317-3476543219
kevin: follow-up: partial DNS weight drift also observed during the same window — some edge nodes had stale geo-weight cache which caused ~10% of traffic to still hit v2 for ~90s due to TTL alignment mismatch. Investigating cache invalidation behavior.
dan: hmm, we changed rollout using central controller which pushes region weights and also triggers a CDN weight flush. looks like eu-west edge responded slower; TTLs at edge were 60s, controller expected 30s. misconfig on rollout tool.
maria: action items: (1) postmortem root cause on mismatch of TTL assumptions, (2) add safety check in rollout controller to validate edge TTL before rolling, (3) update runbook: prefer canary pause and validate for 2m before increasing.
kevin: for immediate mitigation I pushed a targeted rollback of the canary image for eu-west: `rolloutctl rollback service=inference-eu target=eu-west --to=release-20260316-abc123` — that completes at 15:06Z, no errors reported now.
lina: support: 9 of 12 impacted customers reported successful recovery after the flag kill + rollback; 3 still intermittent but improving. Sending follow-up msgs.
maria: does anyone see requests for other regions?
kevin: apac and us-east stable. only eu-west had elevated latency and 5xx.
dan: created a hotfix plan: pin rollout controller to explicit ttl-read in next patch and add a preflight that fetches edge metadata. I'll follow up PR and link in incident.
kevin: adding temporary monitoring alert rule to catch TTL mismatches between controller and edge for 48h.
kevin: logs & traces collected under folder `incidents/3476543219/` and pushed to artifact store.
maria: on-call handoff: i'll stay until initial recovery confirmed. handoff to night-sre (kevin) at 23:00Z. Please include any new regression signals in the incident ticket.
kevin: noted. I'll be primary overnight. If error >2% for >5m re-open pager and start rollback checklist.
lina: drafting customer communication and cc'ing trust & safety.
marco: (from support) any idea which API routes had highest hit? seems `/v1/generate` was majority.
kevin: yes `/v1/generate` top culprit; retries amplified load. we should throttle retries client-side in next SDK patch.
maria: final quick note: no data exfil detected. KMS and logs unchanged.
dan: PR created: https://git.internal/p/rollout-controller/+/987 - includes TTL preflight & safeguard flag.
opsbot: Incident INC-20260317-3476543219 moved to 'stabilized'. Next step: write postmortem and assign owners.
maria: thanks all. I'll file postmortem draft and assign to dan (rollout controller changes) and kevin (observability + runbook).
kevin: will follow up in morning with detailed timeline. locking this thread for updates only. :lock:
